description: CMMC Level 2 Command Registry for M365 GCC High

entries.label: Discover Operator User ID
entries.notes: Resolves the operator's Entra ID object ID by UPN. Captures operatorUserId for downstream role assignment and group membership entries. Evidence proves the operator identity is uniquely identified per AC.L1-3.1.1.

entries.label: Discover Break-Glass User ID
entries.notes: Lookup only (GET, no SET): resolves the break-glass account UPN to its Entra ID object ID and captures breakGlassUserId for the Conditional Access exclusions. A breakGlassUserId supplied directly (TM key break_glass_user_id) is used when the lookup cannot run.

entries.label: Create CUI Security Group
entries.notes: Creates a dedicated Entra ID security group for CUI-authorized users. Group membership gates Conditional Access policies, sensitivity label scoping, and Information Barrier segments. Evidence proves access is limited to authorized users per AC.L1-3.1.1.

entries.label: Add User to CUI Security Group
entries.notes: Adds the operator to the CUI security group. Requires cuiGroupId and operatorUserId captured from prior entries. Evidence shows the operator is enrolled in the access-controlled group per AC.L1-3.1.1.

entries.label: RBAC Role Assignment
entries.notes: Assigns an Entra ID directory role to the operator. Uses roleDefId variable (well-known GUID for the target role). Evidence proves RBAC is enforced, limiting functions to what the role permits per AC.L2-3.1.2. HELD unreachable (phantom control id) pending a founder decision: as planned it grants Global Administrator permanently (DEPTH-1a log).

entries.label: CUI Sensitivity Label and Publishing Policy
entries.notes: Collects sensitivity label and label publishing policy evidence for CUI flow control. In GCC High, CUI flow is typically enforced via sensitivity labels + DLP rather than Information Barriers. Verifies labels exist and are published to Exchange, SharePoint, and OneDrive.

entries.label: DLP Compliance Policy for CUI Flow Control
entries.notes: Collects DLP compliance policy evidence for CUI flow control. DLP policies enforce data loss prevention rules on CUI-labeled content across Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, and Teams. Complements sensitivity labels for full AC.L2-3.1.3 coverage.

entries.label: Service Principal Account Evidence for CUI Flow Control
entries.notes: Queries service principal configuration for the Stamper application. Variable {eoAppDisplayName} resolved from tenant config. Complements Information Barrier entries (ib-segment, ib-policy) for AC.L2-3.1.3.

entries.get_command: $roleId=(Get-MgRoleManagementDirectoryRoleDefinition -Filter "displayName eq 'Compliance Administrator'").Id; $pimPolicyId=(Get-MgPolicyRoleManagementPolicyAssignment -Filter "scopeId eq '/' and scopeType eq 'DirectoryRole' and roleDefinitionId eq '$roleId'" | Select-Object -First 1).PolicyId; Get-MgPolicyRoleManagementPolicyRule -UnifiedRoleManagementPolicyId $pimPolicyId -Filter "id eq 'Approval_EndUser_Assignment'" | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10

entries.label: PIM JIT Eligible Role Assignment
entries.get_command: Get-MgRoleManagementDirectoryRoleEligibilitySchedule -Filter 'principalId eq ''{operatorUserId}'' and roleDefinitionId eq ''{roleDefId}''' | Select-Object PrincipalId,RoleDefinitionId,Status,DirectoryScopeId | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10
entries.notes: Creates a PIM eligible (JIT) role assignment instead of a permanent assignment. Assignments expire after 1 year and require activation with justification. Evidence proves least privilege via time-limited access per AC.L2-3.1.5. Also supports AC.L2-3.1.7 and SC.L2-3.13.3.

entries.label: PIM Eligible Role Assignments for Privileged Users
entries.notes: Evidence-only. Queries PIM eligible role schedules for Global Admin, Privileged Role Admin, and Security Admin. Evidence proves privileged roles use JIT activation rather than permanent assignment per AC.L2-3.1.7.

entries.label: Verify No Permanent Privileged Role Assignments
evidence_commands: $p = @(Get-MgRoleManagementDirectoryRoleAssignmentSchedule -All | Where-Object { $_.RoleDefinitionId -in @('{globalAdminRoleDefId}', '{privilegedRoleAdminDefId}', '{securityAdminRoleDefId}') -and $_.ScheduleInfo.Expiration.Type -eq 'noExpiration' }); [pscustomobject]@{ count = $p.Count; permanentAssignments = @($p | ForEach-Object { [pscustomobject]@{ PrincipalId = $_.PrincipalId; RoleDefinitionId = $_.RoleDefinitionId; Status = $_.Status; DirectoryScopeId = $_.DirectoryScopeId } }) } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5
entries.notes: PH-13 (founder Q3, P13-ST): a count of a bad thing whose honest answer is zero, so the read emits {"count":N, "permanentAssignments":[...]} and is never an empty read; healthy is count 0. Evidence-only. Checks for permanent (non-expiring) assignments on privileged roles. Healthy state is zero permanent assignments — all should be PIM-eligible. Evidence proves no standing privileged access exists per AC.L2-3.1.7.

entries.label: Create Dedicated Admin Account
entries.get_command: $roles = @('62e90394-69f5-4237-9190-012177145e10','e8611ab8-c189-46e8-94e1-60213ab1f814','194ae4cb-b126-40b2-bd5b-6091b380977d','3a2c62db-5318-420d-8d74-23affee5d9d5','29232cdf-9323-42fd-ade2-1d097af3e4de','17315797-102d-40b4-93e0-432062caca18','f28a1f50-f6e7-4571-818b-6a12f2af6b6c','fe930be7-5e62-47db-91af-98c3a49a38b1'); $priv = @(@((Invoke-MgGraphRequest -Uri 'https://graph.microsoft.us/v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments').value) + @((Invoke-MgGraphRequest -Uri 'https://graph.microsoft.us/v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleEligibilitySchedules').value) | Where-Object { $roles -contains $_.roleDefinitionId } | ForEach-Object { $_.principalId }); $bg = @((Invoke-MgGraphRequest -Uri 'https://graph.microsoft.us/v1.0/identity/conditionalAccess/policies').value | Where-Object { $_.state -eq 'enabled' -and @($_.conditions.users.includeUsers) -contains 'All' } | ForEach-Object { $_.conditions.users.excludeUsers }); (Invoke-MgGraphRequest -Uri 'https://graph.microsoft.us/v1.0/users?$select=id,displayName,userPrincipalName,accountEnabled,assignedLicenses').value | ForEach-Object { [pscustomobject]@{ id = $_.id; displayName = $_.displayName; userPrincipalName = $_.userPrincipalName; accountEnabled = $_.accountEnabled; assignedLicenses = @($_.assignedLicenses); followsConvention = ([string]$_.userPrincipalName -match '{adminNamingPattern}'); privileged = ($priv -contains $_.id); breakGlass = ($bg -contains $_.id) } } | Where-Object { ($_.displayName -eq 'Admin-{adminUserName}') -or (($_.privileged -eq $true) -and ($_.breakGlass -eq $false) -and ($_.accountEnabled -eq $true) -and ((@($_.assignedLicenses | Where-Object { $_ }).Count -eq 0) -or ($_.followsConvention -eq $true))) } | Sort-Object { $_.displayName -ne 'Admin-{adminUserName}' } | Select-Object -First 1 | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10

W5c7: a tenant's dedicated admin account is an equivalent when it is privileged, enabled, not break-glass, and either holds no licence or its UPN follows the organisation's stated admin naming convention (adminNamingPattern, from the TM's admin_naming_convention), as EvidenceOps' AC.L2-3.1.6 rule.

entries.label: Configure Smart Lockout (Password Rule Settings: lockout threshold and duration)
entries.set_command: $LockoutThreshold=3; $LockoutDurationInSeconds=900; $s = (Invoke-MgGraphRequest -Uri 'https://graph.microsoft.us/v1.0/groupSettings' -OutputType PSObject).value | Where-Object { $_.templateId -eq '5cf42378-d67d-4f36-ba46-e8b86229381d' } | Select-Object -First 1; if (-not $s) { throw 'Password Rule Settings not found: AC.L2-3.1.8.password-rule-settings creates it' }; $vals = @(@($s.values) | Where-Object { @('LockoutThreshold','LockoutDurationInSeconds') -notcontains $_.name } | ForEach-Object { @{name=$_.name;value=[string]$_.value} }) + @(@{name='LockoutThreshold';value=[string]$LockoutThreshold},@{name='LockoutDurationInSeconds';value=[string]$LockoutDurationInSeconds}); Update-MgDirectorySetting -DirectorySettingId $s.id -Values $vals
entries.get_command: $s = (Invoke-MgGraphRequest -Uri 'https://graph.microsoft.us/v1.0/groupSettings' -OutputType PSObject).value | Where-Object { $_.templateId -eq '5cf42378-d67d-4f36-ba46-e8b86229381d' } | Select-Object -First 1; if ($s) { [pscustomobject]@{ id = $s.id; templateId = $s.templateId; LockoutThreshold = (@($s.values) | Where-Object { $_.name -eq 'LockoutThreshold' } | Select-Object -First 1).value; LockoutDurationInSeconds = (@($s.values) | Where-Object { $_.name -eq 'LockoutDurationInSeconds' } | Select-Object -First 1).value; values = @(@($s.values) | ForEach-Object { [pscustomobject]@{ name = $_.name; value = $_.value } }) } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5 }
entries.notes: DEPTH-10.3 (P12-R2): sets Entra smart lockout on the tenant's Password Rule Settings directory setting (template 5cf42378-d67d-4f36-ba46-e8b86229381d): lockout threshold 3 failed sign-ins and lockout duration 900 seconds, or the organisation's answered values (org_value_bindings; the TM rows for AC.L2-3.1.8 carry them as $.values[?(@.name=='LockoutThreshold')].value lte and ...LockoutDurationInSeconds... gte; only answered values change the command, never weaker than 3 / 900). Every other value of the setting (banned passwords, on-premises mode) is kept. Runs after AC.L2-3.1.8.password-rule-settings, which creates the setting when the tenant has none. Both Graph reads use -OutputType PSObject: on the default Hashtable output, $s.values would be the Hashtable.Values property, not the setting's values array. The read flattens the two values to top-level fields for the registry rule and keeps the values array for the TM's filter paths. GCC High: Azure US Government tenants default to a threshold of 3 and 60 seconds; custom values need Entra ID P1 or higher (G5 includes P2) (https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/authentication/howto-password-smart-lockout, fetched 2026-11-01). Shares the Password Rule Settings object with Entra password protection (IA.L2-3.5.7, banned passwords): this SET rewrites only the two lockout values.

entries.label: Deploy WPA2-Enterprise WiFi Profile via Intune

entries.label: Verify Intune Removable Storage Restriction Policy
evidence_commands: (Invoke-MgGraphRequest -Uri 'https://graph.microsoft.us/v1.0/deviceManagement/deviceConfigurations').value | Where-Object { $_.storageBlockRemovableStorage -eq $true -or $_.usbBlocked -eq $true } | ForEach-Object { [pscustomobject]@{ displayName = $_.displayName; id = $_.id; odataType = $_.'@odata.type'; storageBlockRemovableStorage = $_.storageBlockRemovableStorage; usbBlocked = $_.usbBlocked } } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5
entries.notes: PH-13 (founder Q3, P13-ST): finds the device restriction profile by effect (storageBlockRemovableStorage or usbBlocked true); Graph names device restrictions windows10GeneralConfiguration (no type contains 'deviceRestriction'), so the old filter always read empty. Technical companion to manual gate. Verifies Intune device restriction profiles blocking removable storage.
